architecture.mechanism: Chaotic combustion behavior in spark ignition engines arises from nonlinear dynamics of the combustion process, evidenced by unperiodicity in time series, stroboscopic maps, and a reconstructed strange attractor, where noise levels increase considerably under certain conditions.
architecture.intervention: Redesign the spark plug and ignition timing control to suppress nonlinear chaotic combustion dynamics by stabilizing the combustion pressure time series through optimized spark energy, tighter ignition timing calibration, and addition of cycle-to-cycle feedback control to keep the combustion process within a periodic regime.
architecture.expected_effect: Restored engine combustion stability with elimination of violent sputtering and misfire, stable idle operation enabling A/C cooling, and smooth transmission shifting without recurrence of chaotic pressure oscillations for at least 350 miles of service.
architecture.falsification_test: Install in-cylinder pressure transducers and run the engine over a representative duty cycle (cold start, idle with A/C load, acceleration, steady cruise) for 500 miles; record the pressure time series, compute stroboscopic maps and phase-space reconstructions, and verify that no strange attractor structure or unperiodic intervals appear and that cycle-to-cycle pressure variation remains below the periodic threshold throughout the 350-mile service window.
